hero.badge: Halloween quiz • Solo or as a couple
hero.title: Which supervillain are you most like?
hero.description: Your entrance at the Halloween party, your costume, your lair, your henchmen, your laugh, what you do when someone betrays you or when a hero holds out a hand. At the end, the supervillain you're most like, from the Joker to Maleficent, with their portrait and a Halloween tip. Solo, or as a couple to compare.
hero.subtitle: 15 questions • 5 minutes • solo, as a couple on one phone or each on your own

section1.title: How the quiz works
section1.intro: It's a personality test, but with capes. The questions put you in the villain's shoes on Halloween night: how you enter the party, who your henchmen are, what your laugh sounds like, what you do when you lose.
section1.p1: For example: 'Someone betrays you.' or 'A kid rings the bell: trick or treat.'. Each answer weighs on one or two of the quiz's eight villains. At the end, the villain with the most points wins, and the three traits that stand out most in your answers are shown as gauges.
section1.p2: Solo, you answer the fifteen questions and discover your villain. As a couple, the first player answers the whole series, passes the phone, and the second answers without seeing their answers. Both portraits show up side by side, with the number of identical answers.
section1.p3: Remote mode lets you each play on your own phone: one person creates the game, the other joins with the code, and you see both answers after each question.

section2.title: The quiz's eight villains
section2.intro: We took villains everyone knows, from movies, comics and cartoons, and for each the character trait that sums them up.
section2.pillar1Text: Chaos, laughter, the plan that changes every five minutes.
section2.pillar2Text: Love that's too strong, glitter, and the strength to leave when you have to.
section2.pillar3Text: Cunning, the double game, and the need to be loved behind it all.
section2.pillar4Text: Logic, the plan, and sacrifice in the name of a balance nobody asked for.
section2.pillar5Text: Power chosen after a loss, armour worn like mourning, and the good that remains.
section2.pillar6Text: Control, the fear of death, and the name nobody says.
section2.pillar7Text: Elegance, grudges, and the curse that falls on the forgotten invitation.
section2.pillar8Text: Style, luxury, obsession, and a car driven too fast.

section3.title: As a couple, the question that matters: alliance or war?
section3.p1: When you play as a couple, both portraits show up side by side. Two Jokers is a city that never sleeps again. A Thanos and a Harley Quinn is a lively discussion about what “reasonable” means. And if you want to know precisely which supervillain duo you form, with a role for each of you, that one is played as a couple only.
section3.p2: The other Halloween quizzes are in the same mood: the serial killer you're most like for a darker portrait, which of you dies first in a horror movie for a timer, and who could get possessed for a percentage. The Halloween quizzes and the other holiday ones are all gathered in one place.

section4.title: What you should know
section4.p1: The characters belong to their creators and their studios; the quiz uses them the way you'd use them at a costume party, to laugh at what you recognise of yourself in a fictional villain. The portrait images are illustrations made for the page, not images from the movies.
section4.p2: Nothing is saved: the answers stay on your phone. Only the villain obtained is counted, with no first name or answers, to display one day how the results are distributed on the page.

seo.faq1A: Eight: the Joker, Harley Quinn, Loki, Thanos, Darth Vader, Voldemort, Maleficent and Cruella de Vil. Each one matches a character trait the questions measure.
seo.faq2A: Each answer gives one or two points to one or two villains. At the end, each villain is compared to the maximum it could receive, and the one with the highest percentage wins. The three most present traits show up under the result.
seo.faq3Q: Can you take it as a couple?
seo.faq3A: Yes, taking turns on the same phone, or each on your own with remote mode. Both portraits show up side by side at the end.
seo.faq4Q: What's the difference with the supervillain duo quiz?
seo.faq4A: Here, each of you gets your own villain. The duo quiz gives each of you a role (the brains, the chaos, the muscle, the charm, the shadow, the heart) and the famous duo those two roles form together. It's played as a couple only.
seo.faq5A: No. The answers stay on your phone. Only the villain obtained is counted, with no first name, for the distribution of results.
